source: make an very very very long obbys tiger themed and don't just make it jumps make it wallhops and more

answers.ask: Long as in a tall tower you spiral up, or long as in a flat course that just keeps going?
answers.answer: Make it a very long flat course that keeps going, with tiger-themed sections along the way.

answers.ask: 'And more' beyond wallhops - moving platforms, disappearing platforms, tightropes, conveyors?
answers.answer: Include moving platforms, disappearing platforms, tightropes, and conveyors alongside wallhops so it is not only simple jumps.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] shape — Q: Long as in a tall tower you spiral up, or long as in a flat course that just keeps going? A: Make it a very long flat course that keeps going, with tiger-themed sections along the way.
- [author] options — Q: 'And more' beyond wallhops - moving platforms, disappearing platforms, tightropes, conveyors? A: Include moving platforms, disappearing platforms, tightropes, and conveyors alongside wallhops so it is not only simple jumps.
- [agent_inferred] endpoint — Q: Does the very long course have a final endpoint? A: Make it finite, with one clearly marked finish after the last tiger-themed section.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a very long, mostly horizontal tiger-themed obby made of sequential sections. Keep simple jumps as only one part of the route, alternating them with wallhop sections, moving platforms, disappearing platforms, tightropes, and conveyors. Use bold orange, black, white, and striped tiger motifs to distinguish successive sections while preserving clear obstacle silhouettes and landing surfaces. Lay the course out as one continuous finite route with safe checkpoint pads between major sections and a clearly visible tiger-themed reward area at the final endpoint.

## Genre
The genre is Obby & Platformer, canonical slug `obby-platformer`, because player-controlled obstacle traversal is the whole game.

## Shape and preset
Use `course-flat`, Path (Flat Course), as confirmed: the route advances horizontally rather than climbing a tower. The matched preset is Classic Obby, expanded with the author's wallhops, disappearing platforms, tightropes, and conveyors.

## Config requirements
Use `path-track` for the one continuous ordered platform route, `obstacle-jump` for the ordinary jump sections, `obstacle-moving` for moving platforms and conveyors, `obstacle-timing` for disappearing platforms, and `obstacle-climb` for tightropes and tiger-striped wallhop or wall-scramble sections. Use the visible half of `checkpoint-respawn` for safe tiger-themed landing pads between major sections and the visible half of `winner-zone` for the terminal reward area.

## Layout requirements
Place `checkpoint-respawn` Checkpoints on safe enclosed pads after every major obstacle section, with extra recovery immediately after wallhops and disappearing-platform runs. Place one `winner-zone` WinnerZone at the exact end of the final tiger-themed section. The wallhop geometry is author-specified but may rely on undocumented movement timing, so it must be playtested rather than assumed valid from standard jump metrics.

## Layout components
The build contains one very long flat course, a sequential chain of tiger-themed sections, simple jumps, wallhop walls, moving platforms, disappearing platforms, tightropes, conveyors, safe checkpoint pads, and one final reward zone. Open air surrounds the traversable chain and forms the failure boundary. Compose the route in a long readable progression, with each obstacle family visually distinct.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: draw the complete ordered route and safe landing sequence first, then dress it with tiger styling in isometric form. The top-down plan is authoritative because broken ordering or impossible gaps would make the obby unplayable, while this non-maze, non-racing course does not support `authored_plan`.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale is large, driven by the repeatedly emphasized length and many obstacle sections while retaining individual platforms as readable detail. The theme is a bold, playful tiger pattern in orange, black, and white. Use `P6` because the full course, checkpoint order, and standard obstacle spacing must be valid by construction; wallhops remain an explicit playtest caveat outside normal validation.
